descripcion_geo: Vast peninsula south of the land of Israel, between the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf and the Mediterranean. Land of incense, caravans and Bedouins.
importancia_estrategica: Source of spices and Arab trade; the queen of Sheba came from Arabia; Paul retired there after his conversion.

historias.titulo: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon
historias.descripcion: The Queen of Sheba (Southern Arabia) travels to Jerusalem to test Solomon's wisdom with riddles and gifts.
Following his conversion into Damascus, Paul retreats to Arabia for a time before returning to Damascus.
Wizards from the East (tradition places them in Arabia) follow the star to Bethlehem and offer incense and myrrh.

personajes.descripcion: He visited Solomon to check his fame; Jesus cites her as an example of one who seeks wisdom (Mt 12:42).
He retired to Arabia after his conversion; There he received the revelations that formed his theology.
Son of Abraham and Hagar; Their descendants inhabited Arabia and are ancestors of the Arabs.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Land of the Nabataeans and the route of incense; cradle of Islam; place of Paul's retreat and possible origin of the magicians.

judaismo.descripcion: Ishmael, son of Abraham, was the father of twelve princes and lived from Havilah to Shur, in Arabia (Gen 25:18).
judaismo.significado_teologico: Ishmael, son of Abraham, was the father of twelve princes and lived from Havilah to Shur, in Arabia (Gen 25:18).

cristianismo.descripcion: Jesus cites the queen of Sheba (Arabia) as an example of one who seeks divine wisdom (Mt 12:42).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Jesus cites the queen of Sheba (Arabia) as an example of one who seeks divine wisdom (Mt 12:42).

islam.descripcion: Islam considers Ishmael ancestor of the Arabs and Muhammad; Mecca, in Arabia, is the spiritual center of Islam.
islam.significado_teologico: Islam considers Ishmael ancestor of the Arabs and Muhammad; Mecca, in Arabia, is the spiritual center of Islam.

historias.descripcion: After his conversion, Paul retreats to Arabia; There he received by revelation the gospel that he would proclaim.

historias.titulo: The Queen of Sheba at trial
historias.descripcion: Jesus quotes the queen of the south (Arabia) who came to listen to Solomon; she will condemn those who reject Christ.

historias.titulo: Hagar and the Sinai in Arabia
historias.descripcion: Paul uses the allegory of Hagar (associated with Arabia/Sinai) to explain the difference between law and grace.

personajes.descripcion: He retired to Arabia after his conversion to receive the evangelical revelation.
Jesus uses her as a model of those who seek the truth, contrasting with those who reject it.
Paul uses it as a symbol of the covenant of Law (mount Sinai in Arabia) versus the covenant of grace.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Arabia was the location of Paul's training retreat; also the setting for the allegories about law and grace in Galatians.

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: Paul retired to Arabia to receive his revelation; model of the time of solitude necessary before public ministry.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Paul retired to Arabia to receive his revelation; model of the time of solitude necessary before public ministry.
